results.message: Explain identify the material with an example.
results.answer: To identify a material, first check what each part of the item is actually made from. Do not rely only on its colour, picture, recycling triangle or plastic code. For example, a snack package may have a cardboard sleeve and a soft-plastic wrapper, so identify and check each part separately. Then follow the instructions for your local collection service; local acceptance can vary.

results.message: 请简单解释辨认材料。
results.answer:
辨认材料时，先看物品本身，而不是只看颜色、图案或回收标志。食物残余、金属、纸、玻璃和塑料属于不同类别；如果包装由多个部分组成，要分别辨认。例如，零食的纸板套和软塑料膜应分开判断。确认材质后，还要查看每个部分的说明和当地 council 的收集规定；不确定时先核对，不要直接放入回收箱。

例子：果皮是食物残余，普通纸板是纸类材料，可揉成团的薄膜是软塑料，不是硬塑料容器。

results.message: Explain notice avoidable waste with an example.
results.answer: Notice avoidable waste by spotting food that could still have been used but is being thrown away. results.message: 请简单解释发现可避免的浪费。
results.answer: 发现可避免的浪费，就是留意那些原本还能使用或食用，却因为被遗忘、计划改变或买了重复物品而被丢弃的东西。先查看家里已有的食材，再决定购买什么，可以减少这种浪费。食物在食用前已经消耗了土地、水和能源，因此避免可食用食物浪费也有助于气候行动。例子：打开冰箱，发现还有胡萝卜和豆腐，就把它们安排进下一餐，而不是再买一份新的。

results.message: Explain connect waste and climate with an example.
results.answer: Waste connects with climate because food requires land, water and energy before it is eaten. When edible food is wasted, those resources are wasted too. Globally, food loss and waste together are linked to 8–10% of annual greenhouse-gas emissions (UNFCCC, 2024). For example, planning meals and using leftovers can prevent edible food from being discarded. Unavoidable scraps can go through a suitable organics collection, although this cannot undo the resources already used. This kind of climate education supports SDG 13.3.

results.message: 请简单解释联系浪费与气候。
results.answer: 食物浪费与气候有关，因为食物在生产、运输和储存过程中需要土地、水和能源；食物被浪费时，这些投入也被浪费。UNFCCC指出，全球年度温室气体排放中约有8%—10%与食物损失和浪费有关（两者合计）。例如，本周可以先计划购买分量，并优先吃掉容易变质的食物，减少可避免的浪费。这类学习和行动也符合可持续发展目标13.3关于气候教育与意识提升的方向。

results.message: Explain read each part with an example.
results.answer:
“Read each part” means do not assume one package has one disposal instruction. Identify the box, inner wrap, lid, tub or jar, then read the instruction for each part separately. A label may say a part is recyclable, recyclable only after preparation, or not recyclable. Follow any condition and your local council’s rules.

Example: for a tub with a lid, safely use the food, remove residue as instructed, then check the tub and lid separately. For a glass jar, check whether the lid should stay on or be removed because council rules can differ. Only separate parts when the instructions require it.

results.answer: Prepare items according to what your local collection service accepts—not a universal rule. results.message: Explain reuse suitable items with an example.
results.answer: Reuse means keeping a suitable item in use instead of replacing it after one use. This can reduce the materials, energy and water needed to make new products. Do not reuse packaging in ways that could create food or chemical safety risks.

results.message: Explain plan with available food with an example.
results.answer: Start by checking your fridge, freezer and pantry. Choose food that needs using soon while it is still safe, then plan a meal around it. Check portions, plan for the people eating, and add only missing items to your shopping list. For example, if you have carrots and half a tub of an ingredient, plan a meal using them before buying ingredients for a new recipe. If your plans change, review perishable food again and store it safely.

results.message: Explain put safety first with an example.
results.answer: Put safety first by following the food’s storage instructions and date limits before trying to reduce waste. A use-by date is a safety limit: do not eat the food after it. Best-before mainly concerns quality, but the food must still have been stored correctly and be in suitable condition. For example, keep perishable food refrigerated at 5°C or colder, and use it before its use-by date rather than relying only on its smell.

results.message: 请简单解释安全优先。
results.answer: 安全优先：先遵循食品标签上的储存和准备说明。Use-by 是安全期限，过期后不要食用；Best-before 主要关乎品质，但仍要结合储存方式和食物状态判断。易腐食物应冷藏在 5°C 或更低温度，冷冻易腐食物应在冰箱或微波炉中解冻，不要在室温下解冻。不要只凭正常气味判断安全性，也不要自行延长 use-by 日期。例子：看到食物接近 use-by 日期时，应在期限前安全使用；超过期限就不要食用。

results.message: Explain prevent surplus first with an example.
results.answer:
Preventing surplus starts before shopping: check your fridge, freezer and pantry, plan for the people who will eat, and buy only what you can use. Keep foods that need using soon visible and make a safe storage plan if your plans change.

Example: if you have carrots and half a tub of an ingredient, plan a meal around them and add only missing items to your shopping list instead of buying more.

results.message: 请简单解释先预防多余食物。
results.answer:
预防多余食物可以从购物前开始：先查看冰箱、冷冻室和储物柜，把仍然安全、需要尽快使用的食物放在显眼处；再根据实际就餐人数和现有食材计划餐食，只购买缺少的份量。这样能减少食物被遗忘或买得过多，也能避免浪费食物生产过程中使用的土地、水和能源。

例如，家里有胡萝卜和半盒食材，就先围绕它们计划一餐，再列出需要购买的物品。
